subject: DPA: custodial boundary, data locality commitments and subprocessor plan
messages:
From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@acmehealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency commitments for Acme Health integration

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the earlier demo — Acme Health is moving quickly and our legal/DPO teams need clarity on a few items before we proceed to procurement:

1) We need a clear statement of the geographic custody guarantee for patient-identifiable payloads. For EU tenants, does Redwood guarantee that model inference and any persistent telemetry remain within EU-located infrastructure except for short-lived operational windows? If so, what is the maximum window and what triggers it?

2) Subprocessors: please attach the current roster and confirm whether any analytics or logging is handled by third parties outside the EU. We also need an SLA-level commitment on notification time before adding a new subprocessor.

3) DPA edits: please send a DPA draft with the residency and temporary cross-border processing clauses called out. Our compliance team prefers to see explicit language about transient hops and KMS controls.

Can you send over a single consolidated package (DPA draft, subprocessor roster, and an operational note describing expected short-lived windows), ideally by next Wednesday? We are targeting contract signature by end of month.

Appreciate it,

Alice Moran
Head of Cloud Integrations
Acme Health

Attachments: none
From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency commitments for Acme Health integration

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Laura and Kim (legal + regional ops) to capture contract language and operational constraints.

Short answer up front: Redwood offers region-anchored deployment with EU-only inference and telemetry by default for EU customers. We support a documented transient processing window for specific operational events (failover, cache warm, emergency migrations) that is limited, auditable, and subject to contractual bounds. Ill attach the DPA draft and the current subprocessor roster; below is a concise operational summary:

- Standard guarantee: inference and persisted telemetry remain in EU data centers for EU tenants.
- Transient processing: up to 72 hours per event for limited operational activities (e.g., cross-region cache rehydration or emergency remediation); these events are logged and customers are notified within 24 hours when feasible.
- KMS: customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) or use Redwood-managed keys; DPA language differentiates controls and key escrow.
- Subprocessor notification: Redwood provides a 30-day advance notice for non-critical additions; for emergency replacements a 72-hour notification window is proposed with post-facto evidence and an opt-out right in the DPA.

Attachments: DPA_AcmeHealth_v3.pdf, subprocessors_roster_20260618.xlsx, region_pin_playbook.docx

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm the wording we should surface for the "transient processing" clause (max window, notification, auditability)? Kim, can you add an ops appendix describing what triggers a transient window and the telemetry we capture? I will combine into a single folder and return to Alice by COB Tuesday.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency commitments for Acme Health integration

Thanks Priyom. For DPA language I propose the following draft snippet (sending here so Alices team can react):

"Transient cross-border processing: Notwithstanding the Customer's region-selection and associated data residency commitments, Redwood may perform transient cross-border processing for the limited purposes of emergency remediation, failover, or cache rehydration. Any such event will be limited to a maximum continuous window of 72 hours unless expressly agreed otherwise in writing. Redwood will: (a) notify the Customer within 24 hours of initiation where operationally possible; (b) record the event in an auditable log retained for 12 months; and (c) limit the set of personnel and subprocessors with access to the data for the duration of the event."

Regarding subprocessors: the attached roster identifies which subprocessors operate outside the EU. We can make the following commitments put into the DPA:

- 30-day advanced notice for routine additions; immediate (post-event) notification for emergency swaps with documented justification;
- Right to prior-review: for high-risk subprocessors (security, KMS, analytics) Acme Health may request an independent risk assessment prior to onboarding;
- Escrow: for customers requiring escrow, we can discuss an escrow arrangement or limited subprocessor blackout period while escrow arrangements are established.

I will mark the DPA draft with these points and propose optional text for BYOK vs Redwood-managed KMS options.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

On an operational note Kim: please add a short appendix describing the telemetry we capture when a transient window is opened (identifiers, timestamps, region of processing, subprocessors involved).
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency commitments for Acme Health integration

Laura/Priyom/Alice — added the ops appendix and a short runbook excerpt; main points below (see attached region_pin_playbook.docx for full text):

- Triggers for transient processing: (1) zone-level incident requiring cross-region failover, (2) manual emergency migration requested by customer, (3) automated cache rehydration after global model update when EU edge cache is empty.
- Max continuous window: 72 hours per event, with cumulative monthly cap of 120 hours unless otherwise contracted.
- Telemetry collected: event id, start/end timestamps, customer tenant id, affected resource ids, subprocessors involved, operator username, and justification code. All events generate an immutable log entry and a post-mortem for non-routine events.
- Access controls: limited to SRE/Infra rotation group with privileged audit enabled; subcontractor access is minimized and timeboxed.

Kim
Director, Regional Ops (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
